title: VECOZO
summary: A healthcare application that helps doctors organize consultations, manage patients and work together.

story.title: The Project
text: VECOZO is a Dutch healthcare organization that helps healthcare professionals exchange information securely.
For a school assignment, our team of six worked with VECOZO to develop an application for multidisciplinary consultations (MDOs), where doctors from different specialties discuss patient cases.
We had 12 weeks to build a working prototype that makes it easier to organize consultations, manage patient information and keep everything in one place.

story.title: My Role
text: I was responsible for the entire UI design in Figma, from the overall layout to the reusable components that kept the application consistent.

I also worked on the development side, building core features and connecting the interface to the application's logic and data. Besides my own work, I helped teammates with other parts of the application.

story.title: Behind the Work
text: We were designing for doctors, so keeping things efficient was important. I focused on reducing unnecessary steps and making patient information and common actions easy to find.

On the technical side, I worked with C#, MSSQL and a layered architecture with separate presentation, business logic and data access layers. Getting familiar with C# while understanding how everything connected was a challenge.
We worked in sprints, with two project days each week, and presented our progress to VECOZO every four weeks. Their feedback helped us decide what to improve next.

story.title: The Outcome
text: Together, we built a working prototype that brings patient management, consultation planning and MDO discussions into one application.

I became more confident with C# and gained a better understanding of layered architecture. I also learned how to take ownership of a design while working with a development team and real client. The project reminded me that good software should make people's work easier, not more complicated.

title: MoodTunes
summary: A music discovery app that uses facial emotion detection and personal preferences to generate Spotify playlists.

story.title: The Project
text: MoodTunes is a music discovery app that uses facial emotion detection and Spotify to create personalized playlists.
The idea was to go beyond simply matching music to someone's mood. After detecting how they feel, the app lets them choose whether they want music that matches that feeling or helps change it.
I came up with the concept and pitched it to my classmates. We decided to bring it to life together as a school project.

story.title: My Role
text: I worked on the UI design with another classmate and was responsible for the overall frontend styling, bringing the playful colors, typography and interactions into the application.
I also implemented the Spotify API integration and built the user-choice functionality. Another teammate handled the facial emotion detection.

story.title: Behind the Work
text: Someone's current mood isn't always how they want to feel. If someone feels sad, they might want uplifting music rather than songs that match their sadness. That's why we gave users a choice before generating their playlist.

My main technical challenge was integrating Spotify and connecting the user's preferences to the playlist generation. I also worked on keeping the experience consistent and easy to follow across the different screens.

story.title: The Outcome
text: We built a working prototype that combines facial emotion detection, user preferences and Spotify playlist generation.

I gained more experience working with external APIs and building interactive frontend features. Seeing an idea I came up with turn into a working application was especially rewarding, and it taught me how much a team can achieve by combining different skills.
